extraction_text: 天乘 (Sharmishtha) and her companions, including her servant 多福 (Devayani), went to a forest area for recreation.
迅行王 (Yayati) arrived at the same location while hunting deer and seeking water.
迅行王 (Yayati) saw 天乘 (Sharmishtha) and 多福 (Devayani) with their companions and inquired about their identities.

天乘 (Sharmishtha) revealed she is the daughter of 太白 (Shukracharya), the teacher of the Asuras, and identified 多福 (Devayani) as the daughter of the Asura king 牛节 (Vrishaparvan), who serves as her personal maid.

天乘 (Sharmishtha) asked 迅行王 (Yayati) about his identity, and he revealed he is King 迅行 (Yayati), son of 友邻王 (Nahusha), and a learned king.
天乘 (Sharmishtha) proposed marriage to 迅行王 (Yayati), offering herself, her companions, and 多福 (Devayani) to him.
迅行王 (Yayati) declined, citing that kings should not marry her due to her father's status as an Asura teacher.

天乘 (Sharmishtha) argued that Kshatriyas (warrior class) are connected to Brahma and urged him to marry her, but 迅行王 (Yayati) emphasized the distinct duties and purity of the four castes, with Brahmins being superior.
天乘 (Sharmishtha) insisted that 迅行王 (Yayati) should marry her because he had previously taken her hand in a ritual (implied earlier context), and she had chosen him as her husband.

Sharmishtha (天乘) declares that her hand, once touched by a wise woman, cannot be touched by another man, and since Yayati (迅行), the son of a sage, has already touched it, she implies he must marry her.
